title: Production Water-Thermal Provenance Publication Readiness Audit
scope: audit-only; no production capability and no energy calculation

findings.subject: trial return seam
findings.finding: kernel_advance_interval returns kernel_result_t and one opaque kernel_candidate_state_t from the same completed trial invocation

findings.subject: candidate transaction identity
findings.finding: candidate carries private lineage, origin revision and t0/t1 and exposes read-only provenance accessors

findings.subject: water result identity
findings.finding: kernel_result_t carries requested t0/t1 and mass origin lineage/revision, but these public result fields are not themselves a non-forgeable provenance token

findings.subject: bottom exchange payload
findings.finding: bottom outward exchange amount and terminal flux are materialized in kernel_result_t before candidate publication and can be paired with candidate provenance at the runtime return seam

findings.subject: soil temperature trial ownership
findings.finding: restricted soil temperature is solved and copied into the same trial physical state before the serialized backend reports solver success

findings.subject: soil temperature field publication
findings.finding: current canonical exposes build_soil_temperature_field_view from a soil_temperature_state_t, but serialized runtime does not publish a candidate-scoped full temperature field at the trial return seam

findings.subject: commit ordering
findings.finding: serialized runtime receives result and candidate before optional accepted-receipt commit; provenance needed downstream must be captured before commit consumes and clears the candidate

findings.subject: accepted authorization
findings.finding: fmr_accepted_commit_receipt_t is the existing post-commit acceptance authority; EB-I11 must not create another commit protocol

findings.subject: drainage and root uptake payloads
findings.finding: node-resolved drainage and root-uptake transfers remain backend/process data and are not yet published as accepted transaction-scoped water-transfer payloads

findings.subject: top-boundary route attribution
findings.finding: aggregate trial mass accounting does not by itself preserve a unique thermal donor identity for precipitation, runon, irrigation, snowmelt or soil-to-surface liquid

required_next_production_seam.location: runtime between successful trial return and candidate commit
requirements: capture non-forgeable candidate provenance before commit
bind only authoritative route payloads materialized by that same trial
publish or expose the thermal field from that same candidate without creating a second committed state
authorize accepted publication only with the existing accepted commit receipt
discard all trial publications on rollback or rejected commit

hard_nonclaims: No EB-I10 owner candidate is treated as canonical authority.
No water-transfer payload contract is added.
No soil-temperature runtime view is added.
No sensible enthalpy or Joule calculation is performed.
No accepted energy ledger is published.
No independent qualification or canonical admission is claimed.
